steps.full:
Eight searches are in, spanning the claim as written, three paraphrases, two negation variants, and a question framing. The neighborhood is stable and thin: every framing returns the same small set of adjacent Hawking-radiation claims, and no search surfaces a node stating the mass-scaling relation itself, in either direction. I can now decide.

Assessment of the neighbors:

- "Microscopic black holes evaporate essentially instantly through Hawking radiation" is a *consequence* of the proposed law, not the law: an exponent of 2 or 4 would still leave micro black holes evaporating essentially instantly given their tiny masses. Different decomposition, so a different claim; the proposed law is a parent premise of it.
- "Black holes emit Hawking radiation" is the broader phenomenon; the lifetime-mass relation is a distinct, more specific proposition.
- The LHC claims and the cosmic-ray rule-out claim are topical neighbors only, with no logical bearing on the scaling exponent.

Both negation searches returned only these same neighbors, so the graph holds no mirror-page either. The proposed canonical form is already terse, neutral, and stated as the positive assertion the physics literature debates ("evaporation time ∝ M³"), so I adopt it unchanged.

The nearest neighbors are adjacent, not identical: "Microscopic black holes evaporate essentially instantly through Hawking radiation" is a consequence of the law (it would hold for a range of exponents, so it decomposes differently) and presumably rests on this claim as a premise; "Black holes emit Hawking radiation" is the broader phenomenon, of which the lifetime-mass relation is a specific quantitative corollary. The LHC-related claims (6ba67402-f4e4-47ac-a60b-cf2e6a3bcd78, 8df4a5b0-e490-41b3-b2f2-c6741a873b41) surfaced repeatedly as topical neighbors but bear no logical relation to the exponent and were not treated as near-misses. Since a claim and its denial are one node, the two negation searches are the decisive check for a mirror page, and neither surfaced one. Novelty is therefore the recoverable error: if a counterpart exists under untried wording, the Curator can merge later. The source asserts the proposition affirmatively, so its stance against the canonically stated form is "affirms". Assessment of whether the exponent is in fact three (it carries subtleties such as the effective number of radiated particle species) belongs to the claim's steward, not to this identity decision.
